extracted.intended_audience: Developers writing Macaulay2 packages and documentation
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and quality criteria for writing Macaulay2 packages, code, algorithms, and documentation (naming, types, APIs, performance, and prose). Includes packaging/submission guidance and examples for publishing articles about packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and Unicode
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for readability. Use Unicode where appropriate, as in names of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid acronyms in identifier names
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid acronyms in identifier names. Prefer unabbreviated English words in identifier names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Names representing types should be nouns and written in mixed case starting with upper case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: CoherentSheaf, NormalToricVariety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package naming convention and pluralization
rubrics_metrics.description: Package names should be capitalized. When a package is named after a specific kind of mathematical object, and especially when it exports a type representing that object, the package name should use the plural form of the object's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: NormalToricVarieties is a package that defines and exports the NormalToricVariety type; this helps distinguish the type (single instance) from the package (collection of tools). Set package names in italic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional-argument naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Names representing optional arguments should be capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existing names when possible. Examples: Verify: whether to check that a result is correct or well defined; Verbose: whether to print extra information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Variable names must be in mixed case starting with lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method function naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Use existing symbols, when possible. Names should be written in mixed case starting with lower case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of existing symbols: dim, length, map. Example method name: normalToricVariety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include type name in method names
rubrics_metrics.description: Method names should not include the name of the type of object expected as argument, since such methods are mathematical abstractions that act on a variety of types of mathematical object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean prefix 'is' for predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: The prefix "is" should be used for Boolean variables and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: isPolynomialRing, isPrimary, isPrime, isPrimitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abbreviations in exported names
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations in exported names should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Correct: "formalDepth". Incorrect: "fD".

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming keys in hash tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use existing symbols, when possible, for keys in hash tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: source and target, as keys for the source and target of a map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve distinction between file names and package names
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve the distinction between file names, such as Foo.m2, and package names, such as Foo. A package is an academic work, consisting possibly of multiple files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set package names in italic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use one type to represent another
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use an object of one type to 'represent' an object of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: don't use a matrix to represent the submodule spanned by its columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor complex functions and introduce types as needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not introduce a function that performs two consecutive operations when it would be clearer to factor it into a composite of two functions. If necessary, introduce a new type to serve as the type of the intermediate result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid testing class equality; prefer instance checks
rubrics_metrics.description: It is usually a mistake to test whether the class of an object is equal to a certain class, because that disables inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of writing class x === T, write instance(x,T).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use optional arguments to avoid many similar methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiplicity of method functions that are simple variations of each other may indicate that simplification is possible if named optional arguments are used appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic efficiency: avoid accidental quadratic behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not convert an order n algorithm into an order n^2 algorithm by repeated concatenation of lists or of matrices. Similarly, do not repeatedly append or prepend something to a list, and do not repeatedly remove single items from a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hash tables are your friend here. Notice also that the for ... list ... command offers a convenient way to make a list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of function arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions should take arguments in increasing order of complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if the arguments are an integer and a module, put the integer first. The argument upon which the function mainly acts should go last.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session-wide package configuration options
rubrics_metrics.description: Package configuration options should be restricted to options that can sensibly be set to a single value for the user's whole session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting user symbols and variables
rubrics_metrics.description: To get a user symbol, such as "x", use getSymbol "x". To get n user variables starting with "a", use vars(0 ..< n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control package load order via imports list
rubrics_metrics.description: To control the order of loading of imported packages ("PackageImports") and exported packages ("PackageExports") while the current package is being loaded, mention the exported packages in the list of imported packages, and juggle the sequence of imported packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packages should not print
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages should not print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors should be indicated by calling the function error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid setting User variables without explicit request
rubrics_metrics.description: A package should set no variables in the User dictionary without an explicit request from the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether your package sets User variables, use listUserSymbols after running some of the code in your package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid use and vars in packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The function use should never be used in a package, unless the ring contains no user variables. The function vars should not be used in a package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid setting user variables when creating a polynomial ring, use QQ(monoid[getSymbol "a"]) instead of QQ[getSymbol "a"]. Any names of variables in rings created by the package that get exposed to the user through returned values should be accessible to the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make exposed variable names accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Any names of variables in rings created by the package that get exposed to the user through returned values, directly or indirectly, should be accessible to the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: So use QQ(monoid[getSymbol "a"]) or QQ(monoid[vars 0]) instead of a := local a; QQ[a].

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sequences for multiple return values
rubrics_metrics.description: When a function should return more than one thing, package the several things in a sequence rather than in a list, because then the results can be assigned directly to several variables with something like (a,b,c) = f(x,y,z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundant parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid redundant parentheses. Write f x instead of f(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't test Boolean values for equality with true/false
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't test a Boolean value for equality with true or false, because x===true is equivalent to x and x===false is equivalent to not x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid use of return and magic numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of return, especially on the last line of a function. The use of magic numbers in code should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not export single-character identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages should never export or protect identifiers whose names consist of a single character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables must not have dual meaning; minimize globals
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables must never have dual meaning. Use of global variables should be minimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer builtin abbreviations and helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: Many things you'll be tempted to type more than once have abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when R is a ring, first entries vars R can be shortened to gens R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block delimiters: use parentheses not braces for grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use braces { ... ; ... ; ... } for blocks of code where you don't intend to make a list. Instead, write ( ... ; ... ; ... ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaks and indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The incompleteness of split lines must be made obvious: break after a comma, break after an operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use a text editor where TAB stops are set to something other than every 8th location on the line, then don't use TABs at all for indentation, as your users will see odd-looking indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace: indentation and operator spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents of regions delimited by parentheses, braces, or brackets that consist of multiple lines should be indented more than the surrounding lines, with the same indentation for every line. Operators should be surrounded by a space character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat: n = n+1; doesn't look so bad, so maybe this should apply just to loose operators. Commas should be followed by a white space (but QQ[x,y,z] looks fine). Semicolons should be followed by a space character, but not at the end of a line. Blank lines are not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation must exist for exported items
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exported data type, method, and function must have a documentation page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each documentation page should have an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of examples and tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose examples that illustrate usage sufficiently, without consuming excessive CPU time. Package functionality should be adequately tested, without consuming excessive CPU time and memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Limits are imposed, but under Mac OS X, they aren't enforced.) Assertions about speed can be written but examples should be reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document return types for methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the type of the return value of method functions so the documentation generator can include those methods in the documentation of the type of the return value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: resolution Module := ChainComplex => o -> (M) -> (...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't put blocks of example code adjacent
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't put blocks of example code adjacent to each other. Merge them, or add some text between them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage forms in docs need not be assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'usage' forms for functions don't need to be in the form of assignment statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation headline conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'headline' of a documentation node should be a single brief phrase (not a complete sentence) and thus can be vague. It should not refer to variables by name, because it can appear in a menu, without the accompanying body of the documentation node.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs section: be complete and mathematical
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 'Outputs' section, provide multiple entries only if the function returns a sequence with several entries in it. For each output value, state not only its type, but what it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: say that 'resolution M' returns a free resolution of M; give a mathematical description of the returned object (it could be vague, clarified in the subsequent description, but it should be complete).

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't reload current package in examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reload the current package in example code, because its source code might not be on the path of the user installing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start sentences with English words; punctuation rules in docs
rubrics_metrics.description: Start each sentence with an English word, not an identifier or a symbol. End each sentence with a period or question mark, not with a colon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To indicate that example code just below is relevant, use English words, not a colon. Don't use Macaulay2 identifiers as English words; learn how to use 'ofClass' so the English word and a hyperlink can be generated from the identifier. Don't capitalize English words such as 'list' or 'tally' unless you intend to refer to those classes. Check spelling and punctuation. All sentences should have verbs and subjects. Be clear about antecedents of pronouns. Use 'if' as a prelude to 'then', but use 'whether' to introduce a proposition. Use standard English punctuation: each use of 'e.g.', 'i.e.', or 'resp.' should be followed by a comma. Don't use a slash (/) as a synonym for an English word such as 'or'. Eliminate redundant words. Choose correctly between 'which' and 'that'. Don't use item numbers as English words. Don't misplace 'only'. Add a comma when starting a sentence with an adverb such as 'Finally'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete commented-out code; prefer code rewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete commented-out code. Rewrite confusing code instead of adding comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should be a space after a comment start sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline option for newPackage and submission cleanup
rubrics_metrics.description: The Headline option to 'newPackage' should be a brief phrase stating the topic of the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove any option DebuggingMode => true or Reload => true to 'newPackage' before submitting for publication or inclusion in Macaulay2. Your users aren't prepared to debug your package.

rubrics_metrics.name: JSAG article submission tips
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing an article for JSAG: cite Macaulay2. Articles present mature software, so the package should have a version number at least as big as 1, and should not be described as experimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors should read the entire article. Always typeset Macaulay2 in italic. Example code used in the article should be correct and not elicit errors from Macaulay2. Don't let long lines intrude into the margin of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology precision (different, terms/factors, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful with word choices: don't use 'different' gratuitously; use 'different from' not 'different than' or 'different to'. Distinguish 'terms' (entries in a sum) and 'factors' (entries in a product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use a comma to needlessly separate the subject of a sentence from the verb. Be clear about antecedents of pronouns.
